 # Business Requirements Document — Gym Class Reservation: Reservation API Extension
 
 ## 1. Purpose
 
 This document is a **change request** for the Gym Class Reservation application described in `BRD.md`.
 
 The gym wants reservations to remain after the application is closed. Visitors want to look up a reservation and cancel it when they no longer need it.

 - a REST API that holds the classes, sessions, availability, and reservations;
 - storage of this data in a file;
 - a reservation code for every confirmed reservation;
 - looking up a reservation by its code;
 - cancelling a reservation by its code;

 - **Availability after confirmation (Section 12):** availability no longer resets when the page is refreshed or the application is reopened. Reservations and availability are stored and remain in effect.
 - **Scope (Section 17):** server-side functionality (the API) and storage in a file are now in scope. Cancellation is now in scope.
 
 All other rules of `BRD.md` remain valid, including the classes, sessions, capacity, prices, the reservation flow, the validation rules, the user-interface requirements, and the rule that no personal data is collected.
 
 ---
 
 ## 3. Reservation Code
 
 Every confirmed reservation receives a **unique reservation code**.
 
 The code has the format `GYM-` followed by **6 digits**, for example `GYM-004217`.

 - session day and time;
 - number of participants;
 - price per participant;
 - total price;
 - status.

 If no reservation exists for the code, the visitor receives clear feedback.

 The visitor can cancel a reservation by its code.
 
 - Only the **whole reservation** can be cancelled. Reducing the number of participants is not possible.
 - A reservation can be cancelled **at any time**.
 - After cancellation, the reserved places **return to the session**.
 - A cancelled reservation can still be looked up. Its status is **Cancelled**.
 - A cancelled reservation cannot be cancelled again. The visitor receives clear feedback.
 
 Example: a session has 4 places available. The visitor cancels a reservation for 2 participants in that session. The session then has 6 places available.
 
 ---
 
 ## 6. Storage
 
 Reservations and availability are stored in a **file**.
 
 After the application restarts:
 
 - all reservations remain, with their status (Confirmed or Cancelled);
 - availability remains as it was before the restart, including changes made by reservations and cancellations.
 
 When the application starts and no data file exists, it starts with the initial availability listed in `BRD.md`.

 - gets the classes, sessions, prices, and availability from the API;
 - creates reservations through the API;
 - shows the reservation code in the confirmation;

# Proposed `REQUIREMENTS.md` — Gym Reservation API Extension

**Status:** Proposed for human review and approval. This document consolidates the mandatory behavior in [BRD.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/BRD.md) and [BRD-Extension.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/BRD-Extension.md). It does not choose technologies or resolve details the BRDs leave open.

## 1. Sources and precedence

The original BRD defines the reservation service. The extension BRD adds an API, file-backed persistence, reservation codes, lookup, and cancellation.

Where they conflict, **BRD-Extension.md takes precedence**. In particular:

- Reservations and availability persist after the application restarts; they no longer reset on refresh or reopening.
- Server-side API functionality and file storage are in scope.
- Cancellation is in scope.

All other original BRD requirements remain in effect, including the class catalogue, prices, sessions, capacity, reservation flow, pricing, anonymity, and no-payment rule.

## 2. Purpose and users

The application shall let a visitor reserve places in predefined gym classes, look up a reservation using its code, and cancel a reservation using its code.

Reservations are anonymous. No account, membership, or personal information is required. The reservation code is the only link between a visitor and a reservation.

The application shall not process payments.

## 3. Classes, sessions, prices, and capacity

The application shall provide these classes and prices:

| Class | Price per participant |
|---|---:|
| Yoga | €8 |
| Pilates | €10 |
| Functional Training | €12 |
| Spinning | €11 |

Each class has three predefined sessions. Each session has a maximum capacity of 10 participants.

| Class | Session | Session ID | Initial available places |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Yoga | Monday 18:00 | `YOGA-1` | 10 |
| Yoga | Wednesday 19:00 | `YOGA-2` | 6 |
| Yoga | Saturday 10:00 | `YOGA-3` | 2 |
| Pilates | Tuesday 18:00 | `PILATES-1` | 8 |
| Pilates | Thursday 19:00 | `PILATES-2` | 4 |
| Pilates | Saturday 11:30 | `PILATES-3` | 0 |
| Functional Training | Monday 19:30 | `FUNCTIONAL-1` | 5 |
| Functional Training | Wednesday 18:00 | `FUNCTIONAL-2` | 10 |
| Functional Training | Friday 18:30 | `FUNCTIONAL-3` | 3 |
| Spinning | Tuesday 19:30 | `SPINNING-1` | 7 |
| Spinning | Thursday 18:00 | `SPINNING-2` | 1 |
| Spinning | Sunday 10:00 | `SPINNING-3` | 10 |

A session with zero remaining places is full and cannot be reserved.

## 4. Reservation flow and business rules

### 4.1 Creating a reservation

A visitor shall be able to:

1. Select one of the four classes.
2. Select a predefined session for that class.
3. Select the number of participants.
4. Review the class, session, participant count, price per participant, and total price.
5. Explicitly confirm the reservation.
6. See a clear success confirmation.
7. Start another reservation.

Before confirmation, the visitor shall be able to change the selected class, session, or participant count.

### 4.2 Participant limits and price

- A reservation must be for at least one participant.
- The participant count must not exceed the session’s current remaining places.
- A full session cannot be reserved.
- The total price is participant count multiplied by the class price per participant.
- No payment is taken.

### 4.3 Confirmation and availability

A valid reservation shall be confirmed only following an explicit visitor action. On successful confirmation, the application shall:

- Create a reservation with status `Confirmed`.
- Assign it a unique reservation code.
- Calculate and return its price details.
- Deduct the reserved places from the session.
- Store the reservation and updated availability.
- Provide a confirmation that identifies the reservation, including its code.

Starting another reservation shall not discard confirmed availability changes.

Availability and reservations shall remain stored after an application restart. The original BRD’s reset-on-refresh/reopening behavior is overridden.

### 4.4 Lookup

A visitor shall be able to enter a reservation code and see the matching reservation’s class, session day and time, participant count, price per participant, total price, and status.

Status shall be `Confirmed` or `Cancelled`. If no reservation exists for a correctly formatted code, the visitor shall receive clear feedback.

### 4.5 Cancellation

A visitor shall be able to cancel the whole reservation using its code.

- Partial cancellation or reducing the participant count is not supported.
- Cancellation is allowed at any time; no cancellation time restriction is specified.
- On successful cancellation, the status becomes `Cancelled` and the reservation’s places return to the session.
- A cancelled reservation remains available for lookup.
- A cancelled reservation cannot be cancelled again; the visitor shall receive clear feedback.

## 5. REST API

The API shall exchange data in JSON and provide these four operations:

| Method and path | Purpose | Success status |
|---|---|---:|
| `GET /classes` | Return classes, prices, sessions, and current availability | 200 |
| `POST /reservations` | Create a reservation | 201 |
| `GET /reservations/{code}` | Look up a reservation | 200 |
| `DELETE /reservations/{code}` | Cancel a reservation | 200 |

The `{code}` path parameter is the reservation code, for example `GYM-004217`.

### 5.1 `GET /classes`

Returns all four classes and their three sessions, with current availability. It does not change stored data.

The response is a JSON array. Each class object shall contain:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | Class name |
| `pricePerParticipant` | whole number | Price in euros for one participant |
| `sessions` | list of Session objects | The class’s three sessions |

Each Session object shall contain:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | text | Fixed session identifier from the session table in Section 3 |
| `day` | text | Day of the week in English |
| `time` | text | Start time in `HH:MM` format |
| `capacity` | whole number | Maximum capacity; always 10 |
| `remainingPlaces` | whole number | Current available places |

Example response (shortened to one class and one session):

```json
[
  {
    "name": "Yoga",
    "pricePerParticipant": 8,
    "sessions": [
      {
        "sessionId": "YOGA-2",
        "day": "Wednesday",
        "time": "19:00",
        "capacity": 10,
        "remainingPlaces": 6
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

### 5.2 `POST /reservations`

The request body shall contain:

| Field | Type | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | text | Required; identifier of the session to reserve |
| `participants` | whole number | Required; at least 1 and no greater than current remaining places |

A valid request creates a `Confirmed` reservation, assigns a unique code, calculates the total, deducts availability, stores the reservation and updated availability, and returns the reservation with status **201**.

The success response shall contain the Reservation fields defined in Section 5.5.

Example request:

```json
{
  "sessionId": "YOGA-2",
  "participants": 2
}
```

Example successful response:

```json
{
  "code": "GYM-004217",
  "className": "Yoga",
  "sessionId": "YOGA-2",
  "day": "Wednesday",
  "time": "19:00",
  "participants": 2,
  "pricePerParticipant": 8,
  "totalPrice": 16,
  "status": "Confirmed"
}
```

### 5.3 `GET /reservations/{code}`

Returns the reservation matching the code with status **200**. It does not change stored data.

The response shall contain the Reservation fields defined in Section 5.5. It may return either `Confirmed` or `Cancelled` status.

### 5.4 `DELETE /reservations/{code}`

Cancels the reservation matching the code and returns the updated Reservation with status **200**.

For a reservation currently `Confirmed`, the API shall mark it `Cancelled`, return its places to the session, store both changes, and return the reservation.

A request to cancel a reservation that is already `Cancelled` shall return **409** and make no changes.

### 5.5 Reservation response fields

Responses from `POST /reservations`, `GET /reservations/{code}`, and `DELETE /reservations/{code}` shall contain:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | text | Unique reservation code |
| `className` | text | Name of the reserved class |
| `sessionId` | text | Identifier of the reserved session |
| `day` | text | Day of the reserved session |
| `time` | text | Start time of the reserved session |
| `participants` | whole number | Number of reserved participants |
| `pricePerParticipant` | whole number | Price per participant in euros |
| `totalPrice` | whole number | Participant count × price per participant, in euros |
| `status` | text | `Confirmed` or `Cancelled` |

The BRD permits responses to contain additional fields, but responses must contain all fields listed above.

### 5.6 Reservation code

Every confirmed reservation shall receive a unique code in the format `GYM-` followed by exactly six digits. For example: `GYM-004217`.

The code shall be included in the confirmation and used for lookup and cancellation. The BRDs do not specify a code-generation algorithm.

## 6. API errors and validation

When an API operation cannot be completed, it shall return an error with the applicable HTTP status and a readable message. The exact JSON structure of error responses is not prescribed.

The extension BRD states that an operation which cannot be completed returns an error and changes nothing. This is a mandatory API behavior.

| Situation | Status | Example message from the extension BRD |
|---|---:|---|
| A required field is missing | 400 | `sessionId is required` |
| `sessionId` is not text or is empty | 400 | `sessionId must be non-empty text` |
| `participants` is not a whole number or is below 1 | 400 | `participants must be a whole number of at least 1` |
| Code does not match `GYM-` followed by 6 digits | 400 | `invalid reservation code` |
| Session identifier does not exist | 404 | `session not found` |
| Correctly formatted reservation code does not exist | 404 | `reservation not found` |
| Participants exceed remaining places, including a full session | 409 | `not enough places available` |
| Reservation has already been cancelled | 409 | `reservation already cancelled` |

When multiple errors apply, the API shall return the first error according to this order:

1. **400 — Invalid input.**
2. **404 — Session or reservation not found.**
3. **409 — Not enough places or reservation already cancelled.**

For example, an unknown session identifier combined with a participant count of zero shall return **400** because invalid input is checked before whether the session exists.

## 7. Persistence and request handling

- Reservations and session availability shall be stored in a file.
- After a restart, reservations and their statuses shall remain, and availability shall retain the effects of reservations and cancellations.
- If no data file exists when the application starts, it shall start with the initial availability in Section 3.
- The application is used by one visitor at a time, and requests are handled one after another. Simultaneous use by several visitors is outside scope.

The extension does not prescribe the file format or the timing of initial file creation.

## 8. Frontend integration

The user interface shall:

- Obtain classes, sessions, prices, and current availability from `GET /classes`.
- Create reservations through `POST /reservations` only after the visitor explicitly confirms a valid reservation.
- Show a pre-confirmation summary with class, session, participant count, unit price, and total price.
- Show the reservation code in the successful confirmation.
- Allow a visitor to enter a code, look up the reservation, and view all required reservation details and status.
- Allow a visitor to cancel a reservation by code and show the result.
- Give clear feedback when an API request cannot be completed, using the error status and readable message.
- Continue to support starting another reservation after a successful reservation.

The user interface shall display the class, day, and time to visitors; they do not need to see session identifiers.

The exact visual design is unspecified. No personal information, account information, or payment information shall be requested or collected.

## 9. Explicitly out of scope

The following exclusions are stated in the original BRD’s **Section 17** or the extension BRD’s **Section 9**:

| Exclusion | Source |
|---|---|
| User accounts | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
| Authentication | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
| Memberships | BRD §17 |
| Subscriptions | BRD §17 |
| Payment processing | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
| Discounts or promotions | BRD §17 |
| Database storage | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
| Live multi-user availability | BRD §17 |
| Simultaneous use by several visitors | BRD-Extension §6 |
| Waiting lists | BRD §17 |
| Personal-trainer scheduling | BRD §17 |
| Cancellation | BRD §17, overridden by BRD-Extension §§1–2 and added in §5 |
| Rescheduling | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
| Trainer management | BRD §17 |
| Email or SMS confirmation/messages | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
| Personal data | BRD-Extension §9 |
| External calendar integration | BRD §17 |
| External APIs | BRD §17 |
| Complex date or calendar calculations | BRD §17 |
| Reducing the number of participants in an existing reservation | BRD-Extension §9 |
| Time rules for cancellation | BRD-Extension §9 |
| Operations for gym staff | BRD-Extension §9 |

The original BRD also excludes backend or server-side functionality in **Section 17**. The extension explicitly overrides that exclusion for the API, stating in **BRD-Extension §2** that server-side functionality (the API) is now in scope. Likewise, cancellation is in scope under the extension despite the original exclusion. File storage is in scope; database storage remains explicitly out of scope.

## 10. Mandatory requirements and open implementation decisions

### Mandatory

The requirements described above are mandatory because they are stated in one or both BRDs, subject to the precedence rule in Section 1. This includes the four API operations, their success statuses and fields, the error statuses and validation order, unique reservation codes, file persistence, lookup, cancellation, and API-based frontend integration.

### Open implementation decisions

The BRDs do **not** prescribe:

- Programming language, framework, or internal project structure.
- API port or address.
- File format or internal storage organization.
- Reservation-code generation algorithm.
- Exact error-response JSON structure.
- Whether responses include additional fields; the BRD explicitly permits them.
- Deployment or hosting arrangements.

These remain implementation decisions. This document does not select among them or add requirements for them.

## Exclusions removed

The original BRD’s backend/server-side exclusion is not presented as a current exclusion because BRD-Extension §2 expressly brings the API into scope; its cancellation exclusion is likewise superseded by the extension.

 2. **404 — Session or reservation not found.**
 3. **409 — Not enough places or reservation already cancelled.**
 
 For example, an unknown session identifier combined with a participant count of zero shall return **400** because invalid input is checked before whether the session exists.
 
 ## 7. Persistence and request handling
 
 - Reservations and session availability shall be stored in a file.
 - After a restart, reservations and their statuses shall remain, and availability shall retain the effects of reservations and cancellations.
 - If no data file exists when the application starts, it shall start with the initial availability in Section 3.
 - The application is used by one visitor at a time, and requests are handled one after another. Simultaneous use by several visitors is outside scope.
 
 The extension does not prescribe the file format or the timing of initial file creation.
 
 ## 8. Frontend integration
 
 The user interface shall:
 
 - Obtain classes, sessions, prices, and current availability from `GET /classes`.
 - Create reservations through `POST /reservations` only after the visitor explicitly confirms a valid reservation.
 - Show a pre-confirmation summary with class, session, participant count, unit price, and total price.
 - Show the reservation code in the successful confirmation.
 - Allow a visitor to enter a code, look up the reservation, and view all required reservation details and status.
 - Allow a visitor to cancel a reservation by code and show the result.
 - Give clear feedback when an API request cannot be completed, using the error status and readable message.
 - Continue to support starting another reservation after a successful reservation.
 
 The user interface shall display the class, day, and time to visitors; they do not need to see session identifiers.
 
 The exact visual design is unspecified. No personal information, account information, or payment information shall be requested or collected.
 
 ## 9. Explicitly out of scope
 
 The following exclusions are stated in the original BRD’s **Section 17** or the extension BRD’s **Section 9**:
 
 | Exclusion | Source |
 |---|---|
 | User accounts | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Authentication | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Memberships | BRD §17 |
 | Subscriptions | BRD §17 |
 | Payment processing | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Discounts or promotions | BRD §17 |
 | Database storage | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Live multi-user availability | BRD §17 |
 | Simultaneous use by several visitors | BRD-Extension §6 |
 | Waiting lists | BRD §17 |
 | Personal-trainer scheduling | BRD §17 |
 | Cancellation | BRD §17, overridden by BRD-Extension §§1–2 and added in §5 |
 | Rescheduling | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Trainer management | BRD §17 |
 | Email or SMS confirmation/messages | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Personal data | BRD-Extension §9 |
 | External calendar integration | BRD §17 |
 | External APIs | BRD §17 |
 | Complex date or calendar calculations | BRD §17 |
 | Reducing the number of participants in an existing reservation | BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Time rules for cancellation | BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Operations for gym staff | BRD-Extension §9 |
 
 The original BRD also excludes backend or server-side functionality in **Section 17**. The extension explicitly overrides that exclusion for the API, stating in **BRD-Extension §2** that server-side functionality (the API) is now in scope. Likewise, cancellation is in scope under the extension despite the original exclusion. File storage is in scope; database storage remains explicitly out of scope.
 
 ## 10. Mandatory requirements and open implementation decisions
 
 ### Mandatory
 
 The requirements described above are mandatory because they are stated in one or both BRDs, subject to the precedence rule in Section 1. This includes the four API operations, their success statuses and fields, the error statuses and validation order, unique reservation codes, file persistence, lookup, cancellation, and API-based frontend integration.
 
 ### Open implementation decisions
 
 The BRDs do **not** prescribe:
 
 - Programming language, framework, or internal project structure.
 - API port or address.
 - File format or internal storage organization.
 - Reservation-code generation algorithm.
 - Exact error-response JSON structure.
 - Whether responses include additional fields; the BRD explicitly permits them.
 - Deployment or hosting arrangements.
 
 These remain implementation decisions. This document does not select among them or add requirements for them.

 # Business Requirements Document — Gym Class Reservation
 
 ## 1. Purpose
 
 The Gym Class Reservation application allows visitors to a local gym to reserve places in predefined group exercise sessions.
 
 The application should make it easy for a visitor to:
 
 - choose a gym class;
 - choose one of its available sessions;
 - choose the number of participants;
 - review the reservation and total price;
 - confirm the reservation;
 - start another reservation if needed.
 
 The application is intended as a simple web-based reservation service for demonstration and review.
 
 ---
 
 ## 2. Intended User
 
 The intended user is any visitor who wants to reserve one or more places in a group gym class.
 
 No gym membership is required.
 
 The application does not require a user account.
 
 ---
 
 ## 3. Available Classes
 
 The gym offers four group classes.
 
 | Class | Price per participant |
 |---|---:|
 | Yoga | €8 |
 | Pilates | €10 |
 | Functional Training | €12 |
 | Spinning | €11 |
 
 Each class has three predefined sessions.
 
 ---

 The initial availability is shown below.

 - the session day and time;

 # Business Requirements Document — Gym Class Reservation: Reservation API Extension
 
 ## 1. Purpose
 
 This document is a **change request** for the Gym Class Reservation application described in `BRD.md`.
 
 The gym wants reservations to remain after the application is closed. Visitors want to look up a reservation and cancel it when they no longer need it.
 
 This extension adds:
 
 - a REST API that holds the classes, sessions, availability, and reservations;
 - storage of this data in a file;
 - a reservation code for every confirmed reservation;
 - looking up a reservation by its code;
 - cancelling a reservation by its code;
 - a user interface that uses the API.
 
 ---
 
 ## 2. Relationship to the Original BRD
 
 This extension BRD **applies when it conflicts with `BRD.md`**.
 
 It replaces these rules of `BRD.md`:
 
 - **Availability after confirmation (Section 12):** availability no longer resets when the page is refreshed or the application is reopened. Reservations and availability are stored and remain in effect.
 - **Scope (Section 17):** server-side functionality (the API) and storage in a file are now in scope. Cancellation is now in scope.
 
 All other rules of `BRD.md` remain valid, including the classes, sessions, capacity, prices, the reservation flow, the validation rules, the user-interface requirements, and the rule that no personal data is collected.
 
 ---
 
 ## 3. Reservation Code
 
 Every confirmed reservation receives a **unique reservation code**.
 
 The code has the format `GYM-` followed by **6 digits**, for example `GYM-004217`.
 
 The confirmation must show the reservation code. The visitor needs the code to look up or cancel the reservation.
 
 ---
 
 ## 4. Looking Up a Reservation
 
 The visitor can enter a reservation code and see the reservation:
 
 - class;
 - session day and time;
 - number of participants;
 - price per participant;
 - total price;
 - status.
 
 The status is **Confirmed** or **Cancelled**.
 
 If no reservation exists for the code, the visitor receives clear feedback.
 
 ---
 
 ## 5. Cancelling a Reservation
 
 The visitor can cancel a reservation by its code.
 
 - Only the **whole reservation** can be cancelled. Reducing the number of participants is not possible.
 - A reservation can be cancelled **at any time**.
 - After cancellation, the reserved places **return to the session**.
 - A cancelled reservation can still be looked up. Its status is **Cancelled**.
 - A cancelled reservation cannot be cancelled again. The visitor receives clear feedback.
 
 Example: a session has 4 places available. The visitor cancels a reservation for 2 participants in that session. The session then has 6 places available.
 
 ---
 
 ## 6. Storage
 
 Reservations and availability are stored in a **file**.
 
 After the application restarts:
 
 - all reservations remain, with their status (Confirmed or Cancelled);
 - availability remains as it was before the restart, including changes made by reservations and cancellations.
 
 When the application starts and no data file exists, it starts with the initial availability listed in `BRD.md`.
 
 The application is used by **one visitor at a time**, and requests are handled one after another. Simultaneous use by several visitors is out of scope.
 
 ---
 
 ## 7. User Interface
 
 The user interface:
 
 - gets the classes, sessions, prices, and availability from the API;
 - creates reservations through the API;
 - shows the reservation code in the confirmation;
 - allows the visitor to enter a reservation code, see the reservation, and cancel it;
 - shows clear feedback when a request cannot be completed.
 
 The reservation flow and the user-interface requirements of `BRD.md` remain valid.
 
 ---
 
 ## 8. Personal Data
 
 The application still must not require or collect personal information.
 
 The reservation code is the only link between the visitor and the reservation.
 
 ---
 
 ## 9. Scope
 
 The following remain outside scope:
 
 - user accounts and authentication;
 - database storage;
 - simultaneous use by several visitors;
 - reducing the number of participants in a reservation;
 - rescheduling;
 - time rules for cancellation;
 - operations for gym staff;
 - payment processing;
 - email or SMS messages;
 - personal data.
 
 ---
 
 ## 10. Implementation Freedom
 
 This document does not prescribe:
 
 - programming language;
 - framework;
 - file format of the storage;
 - port or address of the API;
 - internal structure of the application.
 
 ---
 
 ## Annex — API Behavior
 
 This annex describes how the API must behave. It is the common reference for everyone who builds, tests, or uses the API.
 
 The API exchanges data in JSON format. A **request** is what is sent to the API. A **response** is what the API sends back. Every response has an HTTP **status** that tells whether the request succeeded.

 **Purpose:** the operations are the four requests that the API accepts. Each operation serves one business need: showing the classes, making a reservation, looking up a reservation, or cancelling it.

It calls `POST /reservations` when the visitor confirms a reservation, `GET /reservations/{code}` when the visitor enters a reservation code, and `DELETE /reservations/{code}` when the visitor cancels the reservation. The success status tells the user interface that the request was completed.
 
 | Operation | Business need | Success status |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET /classes` | Show classes, sessions, prices, and remaining places | 200 |
 | `POST /reservations` | Make a reservation | 201 |
 | `GET /reservations/{code}` | Look up a reservation by its code | 200 |
 | `DELETE /reservations/{code}` | Cancel a reservation by its code | 200 |
 
 In `{code}`, the reservation code is placed into the address, for example `GET /reservations/GYM-004217`.

 **`POST /reservations`**
 
 Creates a reservation for one session. The request contains the session identifier and the number of participants.

 **Purpose:** an error is the answer of the API to a request it cannot complete. Each error has a status and a readable message.

 # Development Guidelines
 
 ## Project purpose
 
 Build a small web application for visitors to reserve places in predefined gym classes. Keep the experience simple and suitable for demonstration and review. The implementation includes catalogue data, reservation rules, class/session selection, participant selection, a live reservation summary, and in-memory booking confirmation.
 
 ## Business rules
 
 - Offer Yoga (€8/person), Pilates (€10/person), Functional Training (€12/person), and Spinning (€11/person), with the sessions and initial availability listed in `BRD.md` and `REQUIREMENTS.md`.
 - Each session has a capacity of 10. A reservation must contain at least 1 participant and cannot exceed the session's current available places. Full sessions cannot be reserved.
 - Calculate the total as participant count multiplied by the class price. Do not process payment.
 - Require explicit confirmation for valid reservations. Show a useful summary before confirmation and clear success or validation feedback afterward.
 - On confirmation, deduct the reserved places. Keep deductions for the current browser session, including after starting another reservation. Refreshing or reopening restores initial availability; availability need not synchronize across users or browsers.
 - Reservations are anonymous. Do not require or collect personal, account, or payment information.
 - Keep work within the BRD's scope. In particular, do not add accounts, backend or database storage, live multi-user availability, payments, or external integrations unless the requirements are changed.
 
 ## Structure and coding conventions
 
 - The root contains `BRD.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `Support-Case.md`, `PHASES.txt`, `PROMPTS.md`, `TEST_PLAN.md`, and `index.html`, plus `css/`, `js/`, and `tests/`. Keep the BRD and requirements as sources for business behavior and acceptance criteria; use the phase and prompt records for project history.
 - The implementation uses plain browser JavaScript without a build step or dependencies. No additional formatting or lint configuration is established. Follow the existing code style and avoid assuming tools that are not present.
 - Keep implementation focused on the reservation flow and avoid unnecessary dependencies or unrelated refactoring.

 **`GET /classes`**
 
 Returns all four classes with their price per participant and their three sessions. For each session, it returns the current number of remaining places. It does not change anything.
 
 **`POST /reservations`**
 
 Creates a reservation for one session. The request contains the session identifier and the number of participants.
 
 When the request is valid and enough places remain, the API:
 
 1. creates the reservation with status `Confirmed`;
 2. gives it a new, unique reservation code;
 3. calculates the total price (number of participants × price per participant);
 4. reduces the remaining places of the session by the number of participants;
 5. stores the reservation and the new availability;
 6. returns the reservation.
 
 **`GET /reservations/{code}`**
 
 Returns the reservation with this code, with status `Confirmed` or `Cancelled`. It does not change anything.
 
 **`DELETE /reservations/{code}`**
 
 Cancels the reservation with this code. When the reservation has status `Confirmed`, the API:
 
 1. changes its status to `Cancelled`;
 2. returns its places to the session;
 3. stores the change;
 4. returns the reservation.
 
 When the API cannot complete a request, it returns an error as described in A.6 and changes nothing.
 
 ---
 
 ### A.3 Session Identifiers
 
 **Purpose:** a session identifier is a short, fixed name for one session, that is, one class on one day at one time.
 
 **Usage:** the user interface gets the session identifiers from `GET /classes`. When the visitor chooses a session, the user interface sends its identifier in the reservation request. The API returns the identifier in every reservation. Visitors do not need to see the identifiers; the user interface shows the class, day, and time instead.
 
 | Class | Session | Session identifier |
 |---|---|---|
 | Yoga | Monday 18:00 | `YOGA-1` |
 | Yoga | Wednesday 19:00 | `YOGA-2` |
 | Yoga | Saturday 10:00 | `YOGA-3` |
 | Pilates | Tuesday 18:00 | `PILATES-1` |
 | Pilates | Thursday 19:00 | `PILATES-2` |
 | Pilates | Saturday 11:30 | `PILATES-3` |
 | Functional Training | Monday 19:30 | `FUNCTIONAL-1` |
 | Functional Training | Wednesday 18:00 | `FUNCTIONAL-2` |
 | Functional Training | Friday 18:30 | `FUNCTIONAL-3` |
 | Spinning | Tuesday 19:30 | `SPINNING-1` |
 | Spinning | Thursday 18:00 | `SPINNING-2` |
 | Spinning | Sunday 10:00 | `SPINNING-3` |

 ### A.4 Data Fields
 
 **Purpose:** data fields are the named values that the API receives and returns, for example the price per participant or the number of remaining places. The API uses four groups of fields: Class, Session, Reservation request, and Reservation.
 
 **Usage:** the user interface reads the fields of the responses to show the classes, sessions, and reservations to the visitor. It fills the fields of the reservation request from the visitor's choices. The "Meaning and use" column below explains each field.
 
 Field names must be used exactly as written, including upper- and lower-case letters. "Text" means a JSON string; "whole number" means a JSON number without decimals. Responses may contain additional fields, but they must contain all fields listed here.
 
 **Class** — appears in the response of `GET /classes`, once for each class.
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning and use |
 |---|---|---|
 | `name` | text | Name of the class, for example `Yoga`. Shown to the visitor. |
 | `pricePerParticipant` | whole number | Price for one participant, in euros. Shown to the visitor and used to calculate the total price. |
 | `sessions` | list of sessions | The three sessions of the class (see Session). |
 
 **Session** — appears inside each class in the response of `GET /classes`.
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning and use |
 |---|---|---|
 | `sessionId` | text | Session identifier from A.3. Used to name the session in a reservation request. |
 | `day` | text | Day of the week in English, for example `Monday`. Shown to the visitor. |
 | `time` | text | Start time in the format `HH:MM`, for example `18:00`. Shown to the visitor. |
 | `capacity` | whole number | Maximum number of participants in the session. It is always 10. |
 | `remainingPlaces` | whole number | Places still available. Shown to the visitor; a session with 0 cannot be reserved. |
 
 **Reservation request** — the content sent with `POST /reservations`.
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning and use |
 |---|---|---|
 | `sessionId` | text | The session to reserve, named by its identifier from A.3. |
 | `participants` | whole number | Number of participants to reserve. At least 1, and not more than the remaining places. |
 
 **Reservation** — returned by `POST /reservations`, `GET /reservations/{code}`, and `DELETE /reservations/{code}`.
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning and use |
 |---|---|---|
 | `code` | text | Reservation code, for example `GYM-004217`. Shown to the visitor, who needs it to look up or cancel the reservation. |
 | `className` | text | Name of the reserved class. |
 | `sessionId` | text | Identifier of the reserved session. |
 | `day` | text | Day of the reserved session. |
 | `time` | text | Start time of the reserved session. |
 | `participants` | whole number | Number of reserved participants. |
 | `pricePerParticipant` | whole number | Price for one participant, in euros. |
 | `totalPrice` | whole number | Participants × price per participant, in euros. |
 | `status` | text | `Confirmed` for an active reservation; `Cancelled` after cancellation. |

**Status:** Proposed for review. This plan is based on [REQUIREMENTS.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/REQUIREMENTS.md), [BRD.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/BRD.md), and [BRD-Extension.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/BRD-Extension.md). It describes work only; no implementation has started.

## Current project

The application is a static HTML/CSS and browser-JavaScript project. [index.html](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/index.html) loads [data.js](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/js/data.js), [reservation.js](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/js/reservation.js), [ui.js](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/js/ui.js), and [app.js](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/js/app.js). Reservations currently exist only in page memory.

The browser test page is [tests.html](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/tests/tests.html). The existing tests cover the original reservation flow, but not a backend, API, lookup, cancellation, or persistent storage. The project guidance says there is no Node-based test runner or build step; [TEST_PLAN.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/TEST_PLAN.md) documents the original, in-memory behavior and will need updating for the extension. There is an [AGENTS.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/AGENTS.md); no existing `PLAN.md` or `TASKS.md` was found.

## Plan principles

- Treat `REQUIREMENTS.md` as the acceptance baseline, applying its stated precedence for extension changes.
- Reuse the current catalogue, reservation UI, summary, validation, confirmation, styling, and accessibility behavior where compatible.
- Use API responses and server-held state as authoritative after integration; do not retain the old in-memory reset behavior as the application’s source of availability.
- Preserve requirements unaffected by the extension, including participant limits, pricing, explicit confirmation, anonymity, and no payment.
- Do not select an unapproved server technology, storage format, port, or deployment arrangement.

## Phase 0 — Resolve implementation decisions and establish baseline

**Work**

- Review and approve the open decisions listed at the end of this plan before choosing backend or test tooling.
- Run the existing browser suite and record its actual baseline result.
- Identify existing tests that assert original-only behavior—especially reset-on-refresh and no network or storage—so they can be revised where the extension overrides those expectations.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Required technology and integration decisions are approved or explicitly deferred.
- The baseline test result is recorded; known existing failures, if any, are identified before extension work.
- The implementation and test approach does not assume a server runtime or tooling that has not been approved.

**Dependencies:** User approval of decisions that determine the backend, file storage, API connection, and test environment.

## Phase 1 — Server-side catalogue, reservation rules, and file persistence

**Work**

- Provide the class/session catalogue and initial availability from `REQUIREMENTS.md` using the exact session IDs, names, prices, capacity, and initial availability.
- Implement authoritative server-side reservation behavior: validate a reservation, calculate its total, assign a unique code, deduct places, and record `Confirmed` status.
- Implement lookup data and cancellation behavior: mark the whole reservation `Cancelled`, restore its places, and retain the record.
- Persist reservations, statuses, and availability in a file. Initialize from the BRD inventory when no data file exists.
- Keep request processing sequential as required; do not add simultaneous multi-visitor behavior.
- Keep the data representation and business rules independently testable where the selected architecture allows.

**Acceptance criteria**

- All 12 sessions match the approved session inventory and use the exact extension IDs.
- Valid reservations enforce the minimum and available-place limit, calculate the correct total, and deduct availability.
- Every confirmed reservation has a unique code matching `GYM-` followed by exactly six digits.
- Cancellation restores the full participant count, marks the reservation Cancelled, and preserves it for lookup.
- With no data file, initial availability is correct. Stored reservations and availability can be loaded after a restart.
- Domain tests cover valid and invalid reservations, full sessions, repeated cancellation, and reservation/cancellation availability changes.

**Dependencies:** Phase 0 choices for backend runtime and file format. API endpoint exposure is in Phase 2.

## Phase 2 — Implement and test the REST API contract

**Work**

Implement the four specified operations and JSON contract:

- `GET /classes`
- `POST /reservations`
- `GET /reservations/{code}`
- `DELETE /reservations/{code}`

Implement the specified success statuses, required fields and types, and error cases. Apply the required validation order: invalid input (`400`), missing session or reservation (`404`), then availability conflict or already-cancelled reservation (`409`). Return readable error messages. Failed operations must leave reservations and availability unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- `GET /classes` returns all classes and sessions with current availability and status `200`.
- A valid `POST /reservations` returns status `201` and all Reservation fields defined in `REQUIREMENTS.md §5.5`.
- `GET /reservations/{code}` returns status `200` and the reservation’s current status and required fields.
- A successful `DELETE /reservations/{code}` returns status `200`, the updated reservation, and restored availability.
- The specified input errors return `400`; unknown identifiers/codes return `404`; insufficient availability and repeat cancellation return `409`.
- Error precedence matches the stated validation order. For example, an invalid participant count with an unknown session returns `400`.
- Error responses include readable messages. Their JSON structure is not treated as prescribed.
- Responses contain every required field; additional fields remain permitted.
- Tests verify that failed operations make no changes.

**Dependencies:** Phase 1 domain and persistence behavior; approved API runtime/address decisions from Phase 0.

## Phase 3 — Integrate the existing reservation UI with the API

**Work**

- Adapt the existing class/session selection, participant controls, reservation summary, and confirmation flow to use API-provided catalogue and availability data.
- Replace direct client-side booking and availability updates with `POST /reservations` on explicit confirmation.
- Show the code and reservation details returned by the API in successful confirmation.
- Refresh availability from the API when beginning another reservation, while preserving server-side deductions.
- Handle API failures with clear user feedback based on the returned status and readable message.
- Retain the existing anonymous, no-payment flow and applicable accessibility and responsive behavior.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The UI displays the API’s four classes, prices, session days/times, capacity, and current remaining places; visitors are not required to see session IDs.
- Users can choose and change class, session, and participant count, review the required summary, and explicitly confirm a valid reservation.
- Client-side validation feedback remains useful, and the server rejects invalid or over-capacity submissions.
- Successful confirmation displays the reservation code and enough reservation details to identify the booking.
- Starting another reservation shows current server availability, not reset or stale page-only availability.
- API failures are communicated clearly; the UI does not display a success confirmation for a failed request.
- No personal, account, or payment information is requested or collected.

**Dependencies:** Phase 2 endpoints and an approved frontend-to-API connection arrangement.

## Phase 4 — Add reservation lookup and cancellation UI

**Work**

- Add a visitor flow to enter a reservation code and look up its reservation.
- Display class, session day/time, participant count, price per participant, total price, and Confirmed/Cancelled status.
- Add a whole-reservation cancellation action using the code.
- Display cancellation success and clear feedback for invalid codes, missing reservations, and already-cancelled reservations.

**Acceptance criteria**

- A valid code displays all required reservation details and its current status.
- A correctly formatted unknown code produces clear not-found feedback.
- An invalidly formatted code produces clear invalid-code feedback.
- Cancelling a Confirmed reservation returns the updated Cancelled reservation and restores its places.
- A cancelled reservation can still be looked up; trying to cancel it again shows clear conflict feedback.
- The interface does not offer partial cancellation or participant reduction.

**Dependencies:** Phase 2 lookup and cancellation endpoints; Phase 3 frontend/API integration patterns.

## Phase 5 — Integrated regression, persistence, and documentation verification

**Work**

- Add or update focused tests for the API, persistence, frontend/API interactions, lookup, and cancellation using the approved test approach.
- Update the existing browser tests where old reset-on-refresh or no-network/no-storage expectations conflict with the extension. Retain regression coverage for original requirements that remain valid.
- Update [TEST_PLAN.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/TEST_PLAN.md) and [AGENTS.md](C:/Users/RadeDancetovic/CC-Training/gym-vscode/AGENTS.md) so they describe the approved extension behavior and test procedure.
- Verify restart behavior using persisted data, not merely a fresh in-memory state.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Tests cover all four endpoint contracts, required success and error statuses, field names/types, validation order, and failed-operation no-change behavior.
- Regression tests cover the original class catalogue, prices, session inventory, participant bounds, total calculation, summary, explicit confirmation, anonymity, and no payment.
- Persistence verification demonstrates that:
  1. Yoga Wednesday starts with 6 places when no data file exists.
  2. Confirming 2 places leaves 4 and records a Confirmed reservation.
  3. After stopping and restarting the application, the reservation remains and availability is still 4.
  4. Cancelling that reservation restores availability to 6 and records Cancelled status.
  5. After another restart, the Cancelled status and restored availability remain.
- The full relevant automated suite and the documented manual checks pass.
- Project test documentation no longer describes the extension app as in-memory-only or resetting availability on refresh.

**Dependencies:** Phases 1–4; an approved test approach and environment.

## Requirement coverage by phase

| Requirement area | Planned phase(s) |
|---|---|
| Catalogue, initial places, capacity, session IDs | 1, 2, 3 |
| Reservation flow, participant validation, price, summary, confirmation | 1, 2, 3, 5 |
| Reservation codes and required response fields | 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| Four REST endpoints, statuses, error messages, validation order | 2, 3, 4, 5 |
| File persistence and restart behavior | 1, 5 |
| Lookup and cancellation | 1, 2, 4, 5 |
| API-based frontend, clear feedback, anonymous/no-payment behavior | 3, 4, 5 |
| Sequential single-visitor scope and explicit exclusions | All phases; verify in 5 |
| Regression and requirement traceability | 0, 5 |

## Open decisions requiring approval

The BRDs do not specify these implementation choices. Approval is needed before selecting them:

1. **Backend language/framework and how the server will be launched.** The current app is plain browser JavaScript; project guidance records no build step or Node-based test runner.
2. **API address/port and frontend connection strategy.** The BRDs specify endpoint paths, not host, port, same-origin setup, or configuration mechanism.
3. **File format, file location, and storage organization.** The BRDs require file persistence but do not prescribe these.
4. **Reservation-code generation strategy.** Codes must be unique and exactly six digits after `GYM-`; the BRDs do not define generation or behavior if the available code space is exhausted.
5. **Persistence failure handling.** The BRDs require failed operations to change nothing but do not specify API status codes or UI behavior for file read/write failures.
6. **Automated API/integration test tooling.** Existing tests run in a browser; the project guidance says there is no Node-based or command-line test runner.

**No files were created or modified.**

Work in Agent mode. Prepare the project documentation and development setup for the full assessment, using the existing BRD.md, BRD-Extension.md, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, TEST_PLAN.md, PROMPTS.md and the existing application as the source of truth.

**1. Create these three new files:**

- `CHAT_HISTORY.md` – summarize the relevant conversation history, decisions, approved requirements, and assessment instructions. Do not invent conversations or decisions.
- `COMMANDS.md` – record only commands that have actually been executed, with a short explanation of their purpose. Do not list commands that were merely suggested.
- `NEXT_STEPS.md` – provide the current project status, remaining preparation work, implementation phases, and immediate next actions.
**2. Update existing documentation:**

- `PLAN.md` – create or update the complete implementation plan based on the approved requirements and assessment process.
- `TASKS.md` – create a detailed task breakdown with individual tasks, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and proposed statuses. Include separate fields for AI Review findings and Human Review outcomes.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` – verify it against the original BRD and extension. Preserve the approved requirements and examples. Only correct genuine inconsistencies or omissions, and report any proposed changes.
- `TEST_PLAN.md` – update test coverage for all API endpoints, validation, persistence, reservation lookup, cancellation, availability restoration, restart behavior, and regression testing.
- `AGENTS.md` – update project guidance for the implementation workflow, testing, documentation, and assessment rules.
- `PROMPTS.md` – preserve existing content and add the prompts actually used during this assessment. Do not invent prompts.
**3. Project preparation:**

- Inspect the existing application, scripts, tests, and available runtime.
- Identify technical decisions that must be made before implementation, including backend technology, API port, file storage format/location, and test tooling.
- Do not arbitrarily choose technologies where a decision is still required. Document recommendations and unresolved decisions.
- Prepare a clear implementation sequence so that each phase can be executed and tested independently.
- Ensure the plan covers the complete extension, including persistent storage, REST API, frontend integration, reservation lookup, and cancellation.
**4. Important restrictions:**

- Do not start implementing application functionality yet.
- Do not modify existing application source code.
- Do not delete existing files.
- Do not invent test results, completed tasks, AI Review findings, or Human Review approvals.
- Keep task statuses as Proposed until explicitly approved.
- Preserve existing useful documentation and avoid duplicating content unnecessarily.
**5. Final report:**
List every file created or updated, summarize the changes, identify unresolved technical decisions, and state whether the project is ready to begin Phase 1.

Complete the documentation preparation in one pass rather than stopping after each file.

 # Proposed `REQUIREMENTS.md` — Gym Reservation API Extension
 
 **Status:** Proposed for human review and approval. This document consolidates the mandatory behavior in `BRD.md` and `BRD-Extension.md`. It does not choose technologies or resolve details the BRDs leave open.
 
 ## 1. Sources and precedence
 
 The original BRD defines the reservation service. The extension BRD adds an API, file-backed persistence, reservation codes, lookup, and cancellation.
 
 Where they conflict, **BRD-Extension.md takes precedence**. In particular:
 
 - Reservations and availability persist after the application restarts; they no longer reset on refresh or reopening.
 - Server-side API functionality and file storage are in scope.
 - Cancellation is in scope.
 
 All other original BRD requirements remain in effect, including the class catalogue, prices, sessions, capacity, reservation flow, pricing, anonymity, and no-payment rule.
 
 ## 2. Purpose and users
 
 The application shall let a visitor reserve places in predefined gym classes, look up a reservation using its code, and cancel a reservation using its code.
 
 Reservations are anonymous. No account, membership, or personal information is required. The reservation code is the only link between a visitor and a reservation.
 
 The application shall not process payments.
 
 ## 3. Classes, sessions, prices, and capacity
 
 The application shall provide these classes and prices:
 
 | Class | Price per participant |
 |---|---:|
 | Yoga | €8 |
 | Pilates | €10 |
 | Functional Training | €12 |
 | Spinning | €11 |
 
 Each class has three predefined sessions. Each session has a maximum capacity of 10 participants.
 
 | Class | Session | Session ID | Initial available places |
 |---|---|---|---:|
 | Yoga | Monday 18:00 | `YOGA-1` | 10 |
 | Yoga | Wednesday 19:00 | `YOGA-2` | 6 |
 | Yoga | Saturday 10:00 | `YOGA-3` | 2 |
 | Pilates | Tuesday 18:00 | `PILATES-1` | 8 |
 | Pilates | Thursday 19:00 | `PILATES-2` | 4 |
 | Pilates | Saturday 11:30 | `PILATES-3` | 0 |
 | Functional Training | Monday 19:30 | `FUNCTIONAL-1` | 5 |
 | Functional Training | Wednesday 18:00 | `FUNCTIONAL-2` | 10 |
 | Functional Training | Friday 18:30 | `FUNCTIONAL-3` | 3 |
 | Spinning | Tuesday 19:30 | `SPINNING-1` | 7 |
 | Spinning | Thursday 18:00 | `SPINNING-2` | 1 |
 | Spinning | Sunday 10:00 | `SPINNING-3` | 10 |
 
 A session with zero remaining places is full and cannot be reserved.
 
 ## 4. Reservation flow and business rules
 
 ### 4.1 Creating a reservation
 
 A visitor shall be able to:
 
 1. Select one of the four classes.
 2. Select a predefined session for that class.
 3. Select the number of participants.
 4. Review the class, session, participant count, price per participant, and total price.
 5. Explicitly confirm the reservation.
 6. See a clear success confirmation.
 7. Start another reservation.
 
 Before confirmation, the visitor shall be able to change the selected class, session, or participant count.
 
 ### 4.2 Participant limits and price
 
 - A reservation must be for at least one participant.
 - The participant count must not exceed the session’s current remaining places.
 - A full session cannot be reserved.
 - The total price is participant count multiplied by the class price per participant.
 - No payment is taken.
 
 ### 4.3 Confirmation and availability
 
 A valid reservation shall be confirmed only following an explicit visitor action. On successful confirmation, the application shall:
 
 - Create a reservation with status `Confirmed`.
 - Assign it a unique reservation code.
 - Calculate and return its price details.
 - Deduct the reserved places from the session.
 - Store the reservation and updated availability.
 - Provide a confirmation that identifies the reservation, including its code.
 
 Starting another reservation shall not discard confirmed availability changes.
 
 Availability and reservations shall remain stored after an application restart. The original BRD’s reset-on-refresh/reopening behavior is overridden.
 
 ### 4.4 Lookup
 
 A visitor shall be able to enter a reservation code and see the matching reservation’s class, session day and time, participant count, price per participant, total price, and status.
 
 Status shall be `Confirmed` or `Cancelled`. If no reservation exists for a correctly formatted code, the visitor shall receive clear feedback.
 
 ### 4.5 Cancellation
 
 A visitor shall be able to cancel the whole reservation using its code.
 
 - Partial cancellation or reducing the participant count is not supported.
 - Cancellation is allowed at any time; no cancellation time restriction is specified.
 - On successful cancellation, the status becomes `Cancelled` and the reservation’s places return to the session.
 - A cancelled reservation remains available for lookup.
 - A cancelled reservation cannot be cancelled again; the visitor shall receive clear feedback.
 
 ## 5. REST API
 
 The API shall exchange data in JSON and provide these four operations:
 
 | Method and path | Purpose | Success status |
 |---|---|---:|
 | `GET /classes` | Return classes, prices, sessions, and current availability | 200 |
 | `POST /reservations` | Create a reservation | 201 |
 | `GET /reservations/{code}` | Look up a reservation | 200 |
 | `DELETE /reservations/{code}` | Cancel a reservation | 200 |
 
 The `{code}` path parameter is the reservation code, for example `GYM-004217`.
 
 ### 5.1 `GET /classes`
 
 Returns all four classes and their three sessions, with current availability. It does not change stored data.
 
 The response is a JSON array. Each class object shall contain:
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `name` | text | Class name |
 | `pricePerParticipant` | whole number | Price in euros for one participant |
 | `sessions` | list of Session objects | The class’s three sessions |
 
 Each Session object shall contain:
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `sessionId` | text | Fixed session identifier from the session table in Section 3 |
 | `day` | text | Day of the week in English |
 | `time` | text | Start time in `HH:MM` format |
 | `capacity` | whole number | Maximum capacity; always 10 |
 | `remainingPlaces` | whole number | Current available places |
 
 Example response (shortened to one class and one session):
 
 ```json
 [
   {
     "name": "Yoga",
     "pricePerParticipant": 8,
     "sessions": [
       {
         "sessionId": "YOGA-2",
         "day": "Wednesday",
         "time": "19:00",
         "capacity": 10,
         "remainingPlaces": 6
       }
     ]
   }
 ]
 ```
 
 ### 5.2 `POST /reservations`
 
 The request body shall contain:
 
 | Field | Type | Requirement |
 |---|---|---|
 | `sessionId` | text | Required; identifier of the session to reserve |
 | `participants` | whole number | Required; at least 1 and no greater than current remaining places |
 
 A valid request creates a `Confirmed` reservation, assigns a unique code, calculates the total, deducts availability, stores the reservation and updated availability, and returns the reservation with status **201**.
 
 The success response shall contain the Reservation fields defined in Section 5.5.
 
 Example request:
 
 ```json
 {
   "sessionId": "YOGA-2",
   "participants": 2
 }
 ```
 
 Example successful response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "code": "GYM-004217",
   "className": "Yoga",
   "sessionId": "YOGA-2",
   "day": "Wednesday",
   "time": "19:00",
   "participants": 2,
   "pricePerParticipant": 8,
   "totalPrice": 16,
   "status": "Confirmed"
 }

 ```
 
 ### 5.3 `GET /reservations/{code}`
 
 Returns the reservation matching the code with status **200**. It does not change stored data.
 
 The response shall contain the Reservation fields defined in Section 5.5. It may return either `Confirmed` or `Cancelled` status.
 
 ### 5.4 `DELETE /reservations/{code}`
 
 Cancels the reservation matching the code and returns the updated Reservation with status **200**.
 
 For a reservation currently `Confirmed`, the API shall mark it `Cancelled`, return its places to the session, store both changes, and return the reservation.
 
 A request to cancel a reservation that is already `Cancelled` shall return **409** and make no changes.
 
 ### 5.5 Reservation response fields
 
 Responses from `POST /reservations`, `GET /reservations/{code}`, and `DELETE /reservations/{code}` shall contain:
 
 | Field | Type | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `code` | text | Unique reservation code |
 | `className` | text | Name of the reserved class |
 | `sessionId` | text | Identifier of the reserved session |
 | `day` | text | Day of the reserved session |
 | `time` | text | Start time of the reserved session |
 | `participants` | whole number | Number of reserved participants |
 | `pricePerParticipant` | whole number | Price per participant in euros |
 | `totalPrice` | whole number | Participant count × price per participant, in euros |
 | `status` | text | `Confirmed` or `Cancelled` |
 
 The BRD permits responses to contain additional fields, but responses must contain all fields listed above.
 
 ### 5.6 Reservation code
 
 Every confirmed reservation shall receive a unique code in the format `GYM-` followed by exactly six digits. For example: `GYM-004217`.
 
 The code shall be included in the confirmation and used for lookup and cancellation. The BRDs do not specify a code-generation algorithm.
 
 ## 6. API errors and validation
 
 When an API operation cannot be completed, it shall return an error with the applicable HTTP status and a readable message. The exact JSON structure of error responses is not prescribed.
 
 The extension BRD states that an operation which cannot be completed returns an error and changes nothing. This is a mandatory API behavior.
 
 | Situation | Status | Example message from the extension BRD |
 |---|---:|---|
 | A required field is missing | 400 | `sessionId is required` |
 | `sessionId` is not text or is empty | 400 | `sessionId must be non-empty text` |
 | `participants` is not a whole number or is below 1 | 400 | `participants must be a whole number of at least 1` |
 | Code does not match `GYM-` followed by 6 digits | 400 | `invalid reservation code` |
 | Session identifier does not exist | 404 | `session not found` |
 | Correctly formatted reservation code does not exist | 404 | `reservation not found` |
 | Participants exceed remaining places, including a full session | 409 | `not enough places available` |
 | Reservation has already been cancelled | 409 | `reservation already cancelled` |
 
 When multiple errors apply, the API shall return the first error according to this order:
 
 1. **400 — Invalid input.**
 2. **404 — Session or reservation not found.**
 3. **409 — Not enough places or reservation already cancelled.**
 
 For example, an unknown session identifier combined with a participant count of zero shall return **400** because invalid input is checked before whether the session exists.
 
 ## 7. Persistence and request handling
 
 - Reservations and session availability shall be stored in a file.
 - After a restart, reservations and their statuses shall remain, and availability shall retain the effects of reservations and cancellations.
 - If no data file exists when the application starts, it shall start with the initial availability in Section 3.
 - The application is used by one visitor at a time, and requests are handled one after another. Simultaneous use by several visitors is outside scope.
 
 The extension does not prescribe the file format or the timing of initial file creation.
 
 ## 8. Frontend integration
 
 The user interface shall:
 
 - Obtain classes, sessions, prices, and current availability from `GET /classes`.
 - Create reservations through `POST /reservations` only after the visitor explicitly confirms a valid reservation.
 - Show a pre-confirmation summary with class, session, participant count, unit price, and total price.
 - Show the reservation code in the successful confirmation.
 - Allow a visitor to enter a code, look up the reservation, and view all required reservation details and status.
 - Allow a visitor to cancel a reservation by code and show the result.
 - Give clear feedback when an API request cannot be completed, using the error status and readable message.
 - Continue to support starting another reservation after a successful reservation.
 
 The user interface shall display the class, day, and time to visitors; they do not need to see session identifiers.
 
 The exact visual design is unspecified. No personal information, account information, or payment information shall be requested or collected.
 
 ## 9. Explicitly out of scope
 
 The following exclusions are stated in the original BRD’s **Section 17** or the extension BRD’s **Section 9**:
 
 | Exclusion | Source |
 |---|---|
 | User accounts | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Authentication | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Memberships | BRD §17 |
 | Subscriptions | BRD §17 |
 | Payment processing | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Discounts or promotions | BRD §17 |
 | Database storage | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Live multi-user availability | BRD §17 |
 | Simultaneous use by several visitors | BRD-Extension §6 |
 | Waiting lists | BRD §17 |
 | Personal-trainer scheduling | BRD §17 |
 | Cancellation | BRD §17, overridden by BRD-Extension §§1–2 and added in §5 |
 | Rescheduling | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Trainer management | BRD §17 |
 | Email or SMS confirmation/messages | BRD §17; BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Personal data | BRD-Extension §9 |
 | External calendar integration | BRD §17 |
 | External APIs | BRD §17 |
 | Complex date or calendar calculations | BRD §17 |
 | Reducing the number of participants in an existing reservation | BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Time rules for cancellation | BRD-Extension §9 |
 | Operations for gym staff | BRD-Extension §9 |
 
 The original BRD also excludes backend or server-side functionality in **Section 17**. The extension explicitly overrides that exclusion for the API, stating in **BRD-Extension §2** that server-side functionality (the API) is now in scope. Likewise, cancellation is in scope under the extension despite the original exclusion. File storage is in scope; database storage remains explicitly out of scope.
 
 ## 10. Mandatory requirements and open implementation decisions
 
 ### Mandatory
 
 The requirements described above are mandatory because they are stated in one or both BRDs, subject to the precedence rule in Section 1. This includes the four API operations, their success statuses and fields, the error statuses and validation order, unique reservation codes, file persistence, lookup, cancellation, and API-based frontend integration.
 
 ### Open implementation decisions
 
 The BRDs do **not** prescribe:
 
 - Programming language, framework, or internal project structure.
 - API port or address.
 - File format or internal storage organization.
 - Reservation-code generation algorithm.
 - Exact error-response JSON structure.
 - Whether responses include additional fields; the BRD explicitly permits them.
 - Deployment or hosting arrangements.
 
 These remain implementation decisions. This document does not select among them or add requirements for them.

 # Development Guidelines
 
 ## Project purpose
 
 Build a small web application for visitors to reserve places in predefined gym classes. Keep the experience simple and suitable for demonstration and review. The implementation includes catalogue data, reservation rules, class/session selection, participant selection, a live reservation summary, and in-memory booking confirmation.
 
 ## Business rules
 
 - Offer Yoga (€8/person), Pilates (€10/person), Functional Training (€12/person), and Spinning (€11/person), with the sessions and initial availability listed in `BRD.md` and `REQUIREMENTS.md`.
 - Each session has a capacity of 10. A reservation must contain at least 1 participant and cannot exceed the session's current available places. Full sessions cannot be reserved.
 - Calculate the total as participant count multiplied by the class price. Do not process payment.
 - Require explicit confirmation for valid reservations. Show a useful summary before confirmation and clear success or validation feedback afterward.
 - On confirmation, deduct the reserved places. Keep deductions for the current browser session, including after starting another reservation. Refreshing or reopening restores initial availability; availability need not synchronize across users or browsers.
 - Reservations are anonymous. Do not require or collect personal, account, or payment information.
 - Keep work within the BRD's scope. In particular, do not add accounts, backend or database storage, live multi-user availability, payments, or external integrations unless the requirements are changed.
 
 ## Structure and coding conventions
 
 - The root contains `BRD.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `Support-Case.md`, `PHASES.txt`, `PROMPTS.md`, `TEST_PLAN.md`, and `index.html`, plus `css/`, `js/`, and `tests/`. Keep the BRD and requirements as sources for business behavior and acceptance criteria; use the phase and prompt records for project history.
 - The implementation uses plain browser JavaScript without a build step or dependencies. No additional formatting or lint configuration is established. Follow the existing code style and avoid assuming tools that are not present.
 - Keep implementation focused on the reservation flow and avoid unnecessary dependencies or unrelated refactoring.
 
 ## Testing and verification
 
 - Automated tests run in the browser through `tests/tests.html`; open that file in a browser to run the suite. The application can be opened from `index.html`. There is no Node-based or command-line test runner in the project.
 - Add focused tests for changed behavior and keep the browser test page loading the relevant test files.
 - Use `TEST_PLAN.md` for requirement traceability, manual checks, and known testing limits.
 - Verify changes against the acceptance criteria in `REQUIREMENTS.md`. In particular, test the support-case sequence: Yoga — Wednesday 19:00 starts with 6 places; confirming 2 leaves 4; starting another reservation without refreshing or closing the browser must still show 4. Also verify that refresh/reopening restores initial availability.
 - Check the relevant flow for class/session selection, availability, participant limits, price calculation, summary edits, invalid reservations, confirmation, and starting another reservation.
 
 ## Change scope
 
 - Make only changes needed for the requested work. Do not modify unrelated files or broaden scope beyond the BRD and approved requirements.
 - Preserve existing user changes. Review the changes made for the task and ensure unrelated files are not included.
 
 ## Git practices
 
 - Make small, meaningful commits with messages that describe one logical change.
 - Keep each commit focused; do not include unrelated files or changes.
 - Do not commit unless explicitly requested.

 # Project Prompt Record
 
 Record significant AI prompts used during project development and the resulting changes. Preserve the actual prompt text; summarize outcomes factually and do not log prompts or work that did not occur.
 
 ## 1. Create `REQUIREMENTS.md`
 
 **Purpose:** Derive a requirements document from the BRD and support case.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > Read `BRD.md` and the `support-case` file in the project folder.
 >
 > Create `REQUIREMENTS.md` in the project root based on both documents.
 >
 > - Extract all business and functional requirements.
 > - Assign unique IDs (FR-001, FR-002, etc.).
 > - Include acceptance criteria for each requirement where applicable.
 > - Use the support case to identify the specific problem, expected behavior, and relevant edge cases.
 > - Preserve the original business rules from the BRD.
 > - Do not invent requirements or modify existing files.
 > - If the documents conflict or leave something unclear, explicitly flag it in a separate section.
 > After creating the file, summarize the requirements and any ambiguities.
 
 **Resulting change:** Created `REQUIREMENTS.md` with uniquely identified requirements, acceptance criteria, session inventory, support-case finding, and an ambiguities/evidence section.
 
 ## 2. Verify and correct `REQUIREMENTS.md`
 
 ### Verify against source documents
 
 **Purpose:** Audit the requirements for omissions, inaccuracies, unsupported requirements, and conflicts.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > Compare `REQUIREMENTS.md` against `BRD.md` and the support-case document.
 >
 > Verify that every requirement is accurately represented, with no missing, altered, or invented requirements. Check business rules, expected behavior, edge cases, and acceptance criteria.
 >
 > Do not modify any files yet. First report:
 >
 > - Missing requirements
 > - Incorrect or incomplete requirements
 > - Requirements not supported by the source documents
 > - Conflicts or ambiguities between the documents
 > Reference the relevant sections wherever possible.
 
 **Resulting change:** The review identified that FR-022 weakened the BRD's “outside scope” wording, the capacity-versus-initial-availability note was not a genuine ambiguity, and the repeated support-case attempt was not recorded. It also recommended distinguishing the support-platform deliverable from application requirements.
 
 ### Ask for recommendations
 
 **Purpose:** Ask how to address the review findings.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > what do you suggest
 
 **Resulting change:** No files were changed by this prompt. The recommendations were to strengthen FR-022, remove the false ambiguity, preserve the repeatability detail, and document the support task separately if in scope.
 
 ### Apply the review corrections
 
 **Purpose:** Make the suggested corrections to `REQUIREMENTS.md`.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > do those changes
 
 **Resulting change:** Updated FR-022 to explicitly identify exclusions as outside scope; added that the client reproduced the behavior on a second attempt; added a separate support-task deliverable note; removed the capacity-versus-availability ambiguity. No other files were changed in that correction.
 
 ## 3. Create `AGENTS.md`
 
 **Purpose:** Establish concise, project-specific development guidelines based on the source documents and current project structure.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > Create `AGENTS.md` in the project root with concise development guidelines for this project.
 >
 > Base the rules on `BRD.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, the support-case document, and the existing project structure.
 >
 > Include:
 >
 > - Project purpose and key business rules
 > - Coding conventions and existing project structure
 > - Testing requirements and how to run tests
 > - Instructions to avoid unrelated changes
 > - Requirements to verify functionality against acceptance criteria
 > - Git practices, including small, meaningful commits
 > Do not invent project-specific tools, commands, or conventions. Inspect existing files before documenting them. Do not modify application code.
 
 **Resulting change:** Created `AGENTS.md` with business rules, current structure and convention constraints, test guidance based on the absence of an existing test suite or test command, acceptance-criteria checks, scope guidance, and Git practices. No application code was modified.
 
 ## 4. Implement Phases 1 and 2
 
 **Purpose:** Implement the catalogue data, in-browser test harness, and reservation business rules described in `PHASES.txt`.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > do you think that you can implement the first 2 phases now?
 
 **Resulting change:** Added `js/data.js` and `js/reservation.js`, plus `tests/testkit.js`, `tests/data.test.js`, `tests/reservation.test.js`, and `tests/tests.html`. The suite contains 50 browser tests for catalogue data and reservation rules. Updated `AGENTS.md` to reflect the new project structure and browser test harness. The Phase 1–2 tests were later run with the Phase 3 suite in the integrated browser; all 62 tests passed.
 
 ## 5. Implement Phase 3
 
 **Purpose:** Add the class and session selection interface described in `PHASES.txt`.
 
 **Prompt:**
 
 > execute phase 3
 
 **Resulting change:** Added `index.html`, `css/styles.css`, `js/ui.js`, `js/app.js`, and `tests/ui.test.js`; updated `tests/tests.html` to include the off-screen UI test sandbox; updated `AGENTS.md` to reflect the interface and test page. All 62 browser tests passed, and the selection flow and mobile layout were checked in the integrated browser.
 
 ## 6. Implement Phase 4
 
 **Purpose:** Add participant controls, live reservation summary, and validation feedback from the Phase 4 specification.
